key_insight: Second-order curvature and displacement corrections predict flames farther from porous parabolic walls, with lower scalar dissipation, wall shear, and wall heat flux but little temperature change.
engineering_relevance: The corrections improve flame stand-off and scalar-dissipation predictions at laboratory-burner Reynolds numbers, especially with stronger injection or longer porous sections.
method: Extend stagnation-point boundary-layer theory using matched asymptotic expansions.
Include curvature, thermal expansion, and displacement of the reacting layer.
Model a detached flame sheet with unity Lewis numbers.
evidence_signal: Comparison with laminar Navier–Stokes solutions showed approximately quadratic error reduction with the expansion parameter in resolved cases.
watch_item: Applicability beyond the idealized laminar, unity-Lewis-number flame-sheet setting requires further validation; this is an asymptotic model, not an AI surrogate.
paper_title: Nonpremixed Flames Near the Leading Edge of Parabolic Cylinders
